title: EmberLake - Hosted Embeddings + Rerank Onramp
summary: Introductory hosted API demo focused on embeddings + reranking for EmberLake's product search. Covered request/response patterns, how Redwood handles rerank scoring, cost/latency tradeoffs, and integration steps. Customer expressed interest in a short pilot with sample latency benchmarks and security docs.
next_steps: Send hosted API quickstart + sample cURL and python snippets (Maya) - by 2026-04-12
Run a 1k query latency/cost benchmark on EmberLake sample dataset (Carlos) - by 2026-04-16
Share SOC2 and KMS integration notes + private deployment checklist (Anika) - by 2026-04-13
Schedule follow-up POC scoping call with infra and search team (Maya & Sasha) - week of 2026-04-20
action_items: Carlos - produce benchmark plan and template (due 2026-04-16)
Maya - send pricing snapshot and quickstart repo link (due 2026-04-12)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-09
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Rivera (Redwood SE), Anika Bose (Redwood SE), Sasha Patel (EmberLake Head of Search), Liam O'Connor (EmberLake Principal ML Eng), Priya Nair (EmberLake Platform Eng), Tom Willis (Product)
transcript_body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check, audio OK?
[00:06] Sasha Patel: Yep all good. thanks Maya.
[00:09] Maya Chen: Awesome. quick agenda — we'll do a live walkthrough of the hosted embeddings endpoint, then show how to wire into the rerank endpoint, and finish with Console and Optimize suggestions for latency/cost. we'll leave time for q&a.
[00:24] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good, we're mainly focused on improving product search relevance and reducing API costs. current stack is Elastic with a custom neural reranker, we are evaluating moving embedding storage to vector db or using hosted embeddings.
[00:39] Carlos Rivera: Got it. to set expectations — Redwood hosted API offers an embeddings endpoint that returns float vectors, and a separate rerank endpoint that accepts a candidate set and returns scores with the option to stream token-level explanations. in practice people do a two-stage search: cheap retrieval (Elastic or vector DB) then call Redwood rerank for top-K.
[01:02] Priya Nair: Quick question — do you host embeddings for customers or do we need to store vectors ourselves?
[01:09] Anika Bose: Right now hosted embeddings are generated per-request and you can choose to store them in your infra or in a partner vector store. Redwood doesn't force vector storage; we have a managed option (like a small index cache) but it's often better to use your existing Elastic or Pinecone.
[01:27] Tom Willis: Curious about costs — if we run rerank on every search result that's expensive. what controls do we have?
[01:35] Carlos Rivera: Yep. common pattern is retrieve 100 candidates then rerank top 10. Optimize provides batching suggestions and automatic prefix/K V cache for repeated queries which cuts token costs and latency. there are also quantization options for models that trade quality for lower inference cost.
[01:54] Sasha Patel: Could you show a sample request/response and how we integrate it into our pipeline?
[02:00] Maya Chen: Sure — switching to a short demo. I'm going to paste a sample python snippet into the chat — apologies if the format is clobbered by the meeting export.
[02:12] Maya Chen: (screen share) here's a curl for embeddings: POST /v1/embeddings model=redwood-embed-1 input="red running shoes size 9" returns a 768-d float array, and metadata like model version and costs. next, the rerank call expects a query + list of candidate doc ids or candidate text tuples and returns a score for each candidate plus a normalized rerank score field you can plug into your ranking function.
[02:46] Liam O'Connor: are the scores deterministic across model versions? we need stable scoring for A/B tests.
[02:53] Carlos Rivera: By default scores can shift with model version. Redwood supports pinning model versions per-route and you can pin a rerank model so your scores are stable. We also have formal rollouts/canary policies in Console so you can test a new model on x% of traffic.
[03:12] Priya Nair: Security — we operate in a V P C and need K M S integration for keys. how does hosted API fit?
[03:19] Anika Bose: For public hosted we encrypt in transit and at rest and we integrate with customer K M S via a hybrid approach for private deployments. If V P C is required we usually recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private which gives a private control plane and direct K M S/H S M options. We'll share the security pack after the call.
[03:38] Sasha Patel: Any compliance docs? SOC2?
[03:41] Maya Chen: Yes SOC2, plus audit logs, role-based access and S S O. we'll send the SOC2 cert and a summary of our audit logging capabilities.
[03:51] Carlos Rivera: back to rerank — here's a slide showing latency vs candidate size (screen). in our tests 10 candidates reranked with redwood-rerank-micro comes in under 50ms p95 in hosted mode for typical queries, but that'll depend on sequence length and whether you include long passages.
[04:12] Tom Willis: That's promising. how do you handle long doc passages? we often store long product descriptions and specs.
[04:18] Carlos Rivera: We do chunking client-side or in retrieval stage — the rerank call can accept a text blob up to X tokens but best practice is chunk and provide top N snippets to rerank. Also Optimize can recommend chunk size and quantization configs.
[04:36] Maya Chen: Quick detour — does EmberLake have any hard latency S L O for search?
[04:40] Sasha Patel: We target p95 under 200ms from click to ranked results in the UI. ideally rerank adds under 80ms.
[04:49] Carlos Rivera: That's feasible with a retrieval-first approach and Redwood batching + cache. We'll detail a benchmark plan.
[05:00] Maya Chen: I'll demo the Console briefly — Carlos if you want to jump in on the routing bits.
[05:06] Carlos Rivera: Sure. (screen) Console shows per-route token costs, average latencies, and tracing. You can set a routing policy to prefer lower-cost model variants for non-critical traffic, with automatic fallback to a higher-capacity model on errors.
[05:28] Liam O'Connor: How do we test fallbacks without impacting users?
[05:30] Anika Bose: Canary deploys and A/B in Console — route 5% traffic to the new model. We also have simulated traffic replays for offline tests.
[05:41] Priya Nair: On data retention — if we send product titles and P I I in queries is there an option not to log?
[05:48] Maya Chen: Yes you can disable logging per-route and redact fields. For added compliance you can run Redwood Private and keep logs in your V P C. We'll include the exact retention controls in the security doc.
[06:02] Tom Willis: Can you show a live rerank example with our sample product dataset?
[06:06] Carlos Rivera: I have a short synthetic sample — I'll feed a query and 6 candidates. show the rerank payload please... (typing)
[06:24] Carlos Rivera: [typing] sending rerank request... response in 0.038s p50, returned scores: Candidate 3 -> 0.92, Candidate 1 -> 0.78, Candidate 5 -> 0.41. the rerank result includes an explain field with top contributing tokens (this is optional and can be disabled).
[06:48] Sasha Patel: the explain looks noisy — how reliable is it?
[06:52] Carlos Rivera: It's a model-derived saliency, useful for debugging but not a formal proof. some noise expected.
[06:59] Liam O'Connor: For embeddings, do you support different dimensionalities or model families?
[07:05] Anika Bose: Yes we have multiple embed models; you can pick 512, 768, or 1k dims depending on downstream retrieval. Optimize will suggest a model/dim tradeoff based on the dataset size and target recall.
[07:20] Maya Chen: Another question — do you want Redwood to host the vector index as part of the POC or will you run it with your Elastic cluster?
[07:28] Sasha Patel: We'd prefer to keep vectors in-house initially. we already have pipelines to index embeddings into Elastic and Pinecone is not in our stack.
[07:36] Carlos Rivera: Totally reasonable. in that case the common flow is: call embeddings endpoint -> index into your vector store -> at query time retrieve top100 -> call rerank with top10.
[07:48] Priya Nair: What about concurrency? we have spikes during sales events. can Redwood autoscale?
[07:54] Maya Chen: Hosted autoscaling handles typical bursts but for predictable spikes we recommend Dedicated with reserved capacity. Dedicated offers guaranteed GPU pools and configurable autoscale policies.
[08:06] Tom Willis: Any visibility into GPU utilization?
[08:09] Carlos Rivera: Console shows per-model throughput and latency. For Dedicated customers we provide more granular infra metrics including GPU util and per-instance telemetry.
[08:20] Sasha Patel: Can you run a small benchmark on our sample 1k query set to validate p95 numbers?
[08:25] Carlos Rivera: Yep, that's on the action items. I'll run it with your sample and include both cold and warm KV cache runs.
[08:34] Maya Chen: quick note — we've seen customers reduce token costs by ~30% using Optimize suggested batching, and up to 50% with cache hit rates on repeated queries.
[08:45] Liam O'Connor: How invasive is SDK integration? we prefer minimal changes to our backend.
[08:51] Anika Bose: SDKs are simple — it's a couple of HTTP calls. We have examples for node/python/java and sample middleware that handles candidate collection and batching.
[08:59] Priya Nair: Any rate limiting we should be aware of?
[09:02] Maya Chen: Default rate limits are documented per plan; we'll include rate limit guidance for the pilot. If you need higher bursts we can accommodate in Dedicated or with grace periods.
[09:12] Tom Willis: For model drift and quality monitoring — do you provide eval hooks?
[09:16] Carlos Rivera: Yes Redwood Optimize can run prompt-sets/evals and alert on regression. You can tie evaluations to specific routes and get notified when score distributions shift.
[09:30] Sasha Patel: Ok let's talk timeline — we want a quick internal spike within two weeks and then plan a POC if results look good.
[09:37] Maya Chen: That aligns — we'll send quickstart, pricing, and security docs this week. Carlos will run benchmarks when you share sample queries.
[09:45] Liam O'Connor: Anything else on integration complexity?
[09:48] Carlos Rivera: Minimal — main work is orchestrating retrieval -> rerank step and storing embeddings if you choose. We can provide a small reference repo.
[09:58] Maya Chen: wrapping up — any final questions?
[10:01] Sasha Patel: No further questions. thanks for the clear demos. we'll share the sample dataset and schedule the next sync.
[10:07] Maya Chen: Great. We'll follow up with docs and set up the POC scoping. thanks everyone.
[10:12] (call ends)
